items.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I can remember, I can only remember that his name was . . . I can’t think of his first name. Of course his last name was Turner.

ctx.x: Wait a minute. Let’s see . . . Turner. I can remember, I can only remember that his name was . . . I can’t think of his first name. Of course his last name was Turner. God, I can’t remember either of their names. Sorry about that. Maybe it will come to me. [At this point the topic leaps, unexplained, from her grandfather, whom she never met, to an unidentified “he” in the 1970s.] I was living in New York. This was in the seventies, I guess. He would start talking without saying hello or anything. He’d just start…

I’d like to find out, to what degree of importance was each of the following to your family? The first being religion; education, formal or informal; and other traditions and customs. Let’s start with religion.
